description: Canonical end-to-end scenarios. Each one is a CONTRACT WALKTHROUGH: it names the LEGO, capabilities and permissions a flow would traverse, and exists to prove the declared architecture is sufficient to express the flow. None of these scenarios executes today.
purpose: A scenario is the cheapest test of an architecture. If a plausible user request cannot be expressed as a path through the declared LEGO without inventing a new concept, the decomposition is wrong and it is far cheaper to discover that here than after implementation.
rule: Every scenario must be expressible using only LEGO declared in manifest/ai-lego-set.json and capabilities declared in manifest/domains.json. A scenario that needs an undeclared concept is a finding, not a licence to add one.

scenarios.title: Create a company website
invariantsExercised: delegation never widens the parent's capability set
every filesystem and terminal action is workspace-scoped
artifacts are referenced, never inlined into events

scenarios.title: Why did this workflow fail?
scenarios.modeNote: Execution AI is the Copilot's EXECUTION-scoped mode. It is not a fourth engine — the same contracts with the context scope narrowed.
invariantsExercised: a decision summary is stored; the reasoning that produced it is not
memory is retrieved by relevance, never dumped

scenarios.title: Multi-agent coding task
scenarios.joinRule: Parallel branches stay independently observable and join only once their required conditions are satisfied. A join that proceeds on partial results is a different operation and must be declared as one.
invariantsExercised: a child agent's grants are a subset of its parent's
a child deadline is clamped by its parent's
budget exhaustion stops a branch rather than silently degrading it

scenarios.title: Create a node from a description
scenarios.strategySelection: simple -> declarative/template; external API -> connector/OpenAPI; complex reusable logic -> code; heavy deterministic computation -> Rust/WASM.
scenarios.strategyRule: Rust/WASM is selected by measured workload characteristics, never because it is available.
invariantsExercised: a generated node passes the same Node Contract conformance as a hand-written one

scenarios.title: Delegate to an external agent runtime
scenarios.lockInRule: The external runtime stays external and is never reimplemented. Replaceability comes from the adapter contract being stable, not from owning the runtime.
invariantsExercised: an external runtime is not automatically trusted
external events are normalized into the declared 26-type vocabulary before storage

scenarios.title: Record a project decision
scenarios.retrievalRule: A later Copilot retrieves the decision by graph traversal plus relevance. Loading the entire vault is the failure mode this design exists to prevent.
invariantsExercised: the memory graph remains valid with no provider connected

scenarios.title: Token accounting and context rollover
steps: Account for message, model input, output and total tokens
Verify objective, constraints, pending actions, decisions, artifact references and permissions

tokenKinds.message: tokens in the visible message only
tokenKinds.modelInput: everything actually sent: system instructions, conversation, memory, tools, context, current message

tokenExample.note: The UI may show `· 1 token` for the message while the detail view shows the full accounting. Presenting the message count as the model input count is the specific confusion this separation prevents.

scenarios.rolloverRule: Rollover triggers at a declared threshold, never at the exact limit: a rollover attempted at 100% has no room left to write the continuation package.
scenarios.failureRule: If rehydration fails, surface the failure. A silently degraded session is worse than a visible one.
invariantsExercised: a token count the provider did not report is labelled `estimated`
session state never stores the transcript
